text:
sam: quick idea — what if the allocator exposed a lightweight `prefetch_lease` that the scheduler can request before migrating a shard? aim: avoid the 100-300ms cold-start spike when we warm KV caches after an offload.
elaine: hmm, interesting. is this at the page-range level or allocator-chunk level? worried about bookkeeping overhead. :thinking:
devon: can we do it without increasing resident set? prefetch inherently grows RSS. we need caps/eviction hints paired to avoid mem blowouts.
sam: yeah, my thought: lease == ephemeral right to prefetch up to `n` pages; allocator keeps soft quota per-tenant and returns a token. token can be revoked, and prefetch can be best-effort.
ryan: if we make token revocable we need fast path to cancel inflight warms. add `revoke_prefetch(token)` and `prefetch_status(token)` metrics. also instrument `prefetch_success_rate` and `prefetch_cost_ms`.
elaine: API sketch looks like: ```
// request prefetch window, returns token or OOM
string prefetch_lease(range, max_pages, ttl_ms = 500)
// try/cancel
void release_prefetch(string token)
void revoke_prefetch(string token) // allocator or admissions can call
```
devon: eviction/hint integration: allocator should expose `soft_evict_hint(range, priority)` so admission can steer what to drop if quota needed. we already have strong evict flow; this is more cooperative.
sam: agreed. implementation notes: 1) keep metadata off hot path (only token id on allocations), 2) make prefetch asynchronous w/ per-token window, 3) admission controller enforces per-node + per-tenant buckets. minimal ABI surface.
ryan: telemetry + safety: start behind feature-flag, run on small tenant cohort, monitor token revokes vs success ratio. add a fallback to on-demand fetch if too many revokes.
elaine: one more tradeoff — pinned pages vs cached warms. pinned warms reduce thrash but hurt co-tenancy. suggest `urgency` enum: LOW (cache), HIGH (pin briefly).
devon: +1 for urgency. also think about NUMA: prefetch should prefer local node and allow `remote_preferred=false` override.
sam: ok next steps: I'll draft a micro-RFC with API, admission counters, and a prototype patchset (allocator + admissions + runtime hooks). propose canary on one rack. :+1:
ops-bot: deploy-check: prefetch feature-flag gate created in `canary/prefetch-lease` rollout group. CI tests: basic token lifecycle ✅, revoke path flaky (investigating).
ryan: thanks — include dashboard widgets: prefetch tokens/sec, avg prefetch latency, revoke ratio, rss delta per-token.
sam: cool — i'll put the RFC in `eng-runtime` docs and tag you all. short-term goal: reduce migration stalls by 30-50% for small-model bursts.
elaine: sounds good. minimal ABI, reversible ops, and metrics. if the prototype looks clean we can evaluate adding to dedicated pools.
